notes:
Account background: Pyxis Source Labs builds a developer-facing code search platform used by large enterprises. Their product indexes multi-language monorepos (Go, Python, TS/JS, Java) and supports cross-repo code intelligence. Primary pain: current vector store cannot sustain daily re-index of repos and rerank at 200-500 QPS without cost blowup.

Technical requirements (from Eng):
- Embedding scale: plan for 200M-500M vectors in year 1 (site: 5K repos, avg 40K files/repo).
- Index refresh cadence: daily full incremental; hot-path delta updates every 30m for active repos.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end <150ms for top-k retrieval+rerank pipeline (target 100-120ms ideal).
- Throughput target: baseline 300 QPS during business hours; 800 QPS burst for CI/indexing windows.
- Cost target: <= $0.03/query (retrieval + rerank amortized) for hosted-like compare; high sensitivity to per-query unit economics.
- Model prefs: open 2-stage: cheaper retrieval embeddings (768-1024 dims, quantized) + stronger reranker (L2 cross-encoder or rerank model, GPU-backed). Prefer Redwood suggestions on quantization and dedicated pools.
- Data controls: must support SSO (SAML) + SCIM; customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) desired; audit logs 1yr retention; US data residency requirement.
- Network: VPC peering or Private deployment; vendor cannot have access to plaintext repo content — encryption-in-transit & at-rest required.

POC scope agreed: ingest 30M vectors (subset: 150 active repos), run A/B of rerank strategy (approx 2 retrieval models + 1 cross-encoder), measure latency and cost. Canary for rerank fallbacks.
